title.narrative: Emergency provision of lifesaving Shelter-NFIs to returnees from Sudan and host communities in Northern Bahr El Ghazal (Kirr Adem and Majokyinthiou)

description.narrative: ltpgtThrough this First Reserve Allocation, Care for Children Old Age in South Sudan (CCOSS) aims to deliver emergency SNFI services, contributing to the integration and recovery of the newly affected populations (returnees) in Kirr Adem (Aweil North), and Majokyinthiou (Aweil East). Within the framework of shelter and Non-Food Items (NFI) Cluster objectives and sector strategic goals, this project is initiated aiming to contribute in developing shelter solutions and NFI assistance.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtCCOSS proposes to use the standard response methodology. The project will ensure that accurate data is collected, detailed needs, market assessments conducted, consultations with affected communities and monitoring strategies placed to ensure quality programming. The project will identify any HLP and insecurity issues, conduct rapid market assessments and map potential shelters or structures that could be used as temporary reception centers. Upon arrival of the returnees, the project will mobilize and support construction of waiting sheds, provide essential NFIs, facilitate HLP discussions for land allocation and provide shelter construction materials. The project will also train the returnees on how to construct the shelters.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis project while addressing immediate emergency needs, the main aim is to connect these activities to long-term solutions by facilitating reintegration. The project aims to provide Survival Kits /Emergency shelter/Non-Food items both in-kind and in cash modalities to the returnees and vulnerable host communities. The project will focus on the lifesaving shelter/NFIs needs, as identified through assessments to assist with their reintegration into the host community or to start anew, while simultaneously reducing protection and health risks.ltbrgtAlso, the project will focus on supporting transition, recovery and reintegration of returnees, and vulnerable households through provision of appropriate and environmentally friendly transitional shelters and provision of shelter construction materials for self-building or supported with Labor costs for vulnerable households with lack of capacity to implement. Also, Community awareness on the impact of Shelter/NFI activities on the environment and mitigation measures will be reinforced. Addition to this, the project will implement constructive training program on alternate building techniques and technical guidance for effective shelter delivery. Furthermore, the project will support prepositioning of NFIs and materials to support timely response. Moreover, the project will ensure gender and environmental markers, and other cross-cutting issues have been addressed through ensuring that the needs of all beneficiaries are addressed. CCOSS will inform and consult affected population at each stage of the project and will establish complaint and feedback mechanism.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project will consider pregnant women, chronically ill people, elderly, unaccompanied minors, and people with disabilities as highly vulnerable groups. At least 15% of the target population will be PWDs.ltbrgtlt/pgt
